output.summary: KEP-4818 allows a zero value for the sleep duration of the PreStop Sleep action, which the parent KEP-3960 validation rejected. It was added behind the PodLifecycleSleepActionAllowZero feature gate and the KEP reached stable; its status is implemented.
output.rationale: Validation rejected sleep.seconds = 0 ("must be greater than 0"), even though time.After() accepts zero and returns immediately, so a zero sleep is effectively a no-op. Users such as those whose admission webhooks inject a default PreStop sleep need a no-op hook to opt out. The proposal relaxes validation for new resources and updates while keeping existing zero-second resources working during downgrades.

alternatives.why_not: Requires a sleep binary in the image; the sleep action already exists as a PreStop hook, so allowing zero there is easier.

alternatives.option: Support negative values or an infinite sleep as well
alternatives.why_not: Non-goals: negative values have the same effect as zero, and the KEP does not aim to delay pod termination indefinitely.

alternatives.option: Add a kubelet-side feature gate check for zero values
alternatives.why_not: Kubelet already accepts zero via time.After(0), so the sreeram-venkitesh comment judged the gate unnecessary at the kubelet level.

evidence.quote: It however doesn’t accept zero as a valid value for the sleep duration seconds. This KEP aims to add support for setting a value of zero with the sleep action of the PreStop hook.

Introduce a `PodLifecycleSleepActionAllowZero` feature gate which is disabled by default. When the feature gate is enabled, the `validateSleepAction` method would allow values greater than or equal to zero
Currently, kubelet accepts `0`. No validation is done at the kubelet level. The feature gate for `PodLifecycleSleepAction` is used inside `runSleepHandler` function
This KEP is for allowing zero value for the sleep duration and this was in alpha in 1.32.
thank you for updating the history as well! Very thoughtful of you! /lgtm /approve
